allowed_dependency_manifest.content: Let n, k, l ∈ Z with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n. Define R(q) = [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q in the natural rational-function setting for Gaussian q-binomial coefficients. If R(q) lies in a polynomial ring in q (i.e., R(q) has only finitely many nonnegative powers of q with coefficients in the relevant coefficient ring), then when written as R(q) = Σ_i c_i q^i, every coefficient c_i satisfies c_i ≥ 0.

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260324204708_474b5c77
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers A, B, d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q_{A,B,d}(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when d = 0. Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q]. Let S be the weighted polynomial ring Q[x_1, ..., x_d] graded by deg(x_i) = B+i; when d = 0 interpret S as Q. Then there exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that deg(f_i) = A+i for every i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1, ..., f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, Q_{A,B,d}(q) is realized by a homogeneous regular sequence in a weighted polynomial ring with variable weights B+1, ..., B+d and relation degrees A+1, ..., A+d.

payload.statement_nl: Let A,B,d be integers with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0. For j=1,...,d put w_j := B+j and let E := {A+1,...,A+d}. Assume that for every positive integer n, the number of indices j in {1,...,d} for which n divides w_j is at most the number of integers e in E for which n divides e. For each subset J of {1,...,d}, define Sigma(J) := { sum_{j in J} m_j w_j : each m_j is a nonnegative integer }. Then for every nonempty subset J of {1,...,d}, the cardinality of E intersect Sigma(J) is at least |J|.

result_payload.proof_summary:
I could prove a substantial reduction but not the full lemma. Let s:=A-B. When s<d, write W={B+1,...,B+d}=L\sqcup O and E={A+1,...,A+d}=O\sqcup R with L={B+1,...,A}, O={A+1,...,B+d}, R={B+d+1,...,A+d}. Then for every n>0 the given divisibility inequality for W and E reduces to #{x\in L:n|x}<=#{x\in R:n|x}. Hence the smaller interval pair (L,R), of common length s<d, satisfies the same hypothesis. Applying induction on d to the subset J\cap\{1,...,s\} gives at least |J\cap\{1,...,s\}| elements of R in the semigroup generated by those left-hand weights; the remaining indices j>s contribute the distinct weights w_j themselves, which lie in O\subset E. This settles the overlapping case s<d.

What I could not finish is the disjoint case s>=d. In that case one can form
P(q)=\prod_{i=1}^d \frac{1-q^{A+i}}{1-q^{B+i}}=\frac{\bigl[{A+B+d \atop B+d}\bigr]_q}{\bigl[{A+B+d \atop B}\bigr]_q}.
Using 1-q^m=\prod_{r|m}\Phi_r(q), the hypothesis implies P(q) is a polynomial, and then the allowed q-binomial-ratio positivity result gives that P(q) has nonnegative coefficients. I was unable, however, to extract from that positivity the required Hall-type semigroup conclusion for an arbitrary subset J without invoking a substantial external theorem (essentially Hall's theorem on integral factorial ratios / semigroup conditions).

suspected_gaps: I do not have a rigorous argument for the disjoint case A-B>=d.
I could not justify the passage from positivity of the full q-binomial ratio polynomial to the semigroup condition for every subset J without using a substantial external theorem.
used_external_facts: The standard product formula for Gaussian q-binomial coefficients, used only in the partial reduction.

result_payload.stuck_point: After reducing the overlapping case by induction, the remaining case A-B>=d seems to require a nontrivial bridge from positivity of P(q)=\prod_{i=1}^d (1-q^{A+i})/(1-q^{B+i}) to the Hall-type subset semigroup condition. I could not supply that bridge rigorously from the allowed context alone.
